question: What are the two main drivers of gastrointestinal changes during pregnancy?

options.A: Reduced blood volume and low body temperature
options.B: Bacterial infections and dietary fiber loss
options.C: Increased water intake and heavy lifting

explanation: Elevated pregnancy hormones and the growing uterus pushing against abdominal organs cause most digestive changes. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T7#BMP212_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why is it important for midwives to understand normal gastrointestinal adaptations in pregnancy?

options.A: To prevent the baby from digesting maternal food too early
options.B: To prescribe strong surgical interventions for routine heartburn
options.C: To separate normal pregnancy discomforts from actual illnesses
options.D: To stop women from eating local foods during antenatal visits

explanation: Knowing what changes are expected allows midwives to reassure mothers and avoid unnecessary treatments for normal symptoms. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T7#BMP212_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for relaxing smooth muscle in the digestive tract during pregnancy?
explanation: Progesterone causes the smooth muscles of the gut to relax, which slows down digestion. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T7#BMP212_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the main biological benefit of slowed gut motility caused by pregnancy hormones?

options.A: It completely stops the production of stomach acid
options.B: It prevents the stomach from ever expanding too much
options.C: It allows more time for nutrient and water absorption
options.D: It speeds up the elimination of toxins from the liver

explanation: Slower movement through the intestines ensures the mother's body extracts maximum nutrients for the baby. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T7#BMP212_U1_T7_h2)

question: What causes heartburn or acid reflux during pregnancy?

options.A: Complete closure of the upper esophageal opening
options.B: Rapid emptying of food directly into the colon
options.C: Excessive production of thick saliva in the mouth
options.D: Relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter

explanation: When the valve between the stomach and esophagus relaxes due to hormones, acid leaks upward and causes a burning sensation. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T7#BMP212_U1_T7_h3)

question: A pregnant woman at 28 weeks complains of a burning chest sensation after eating heavy meals. What underlying process is most likely happening?

options.A: Her stomach is digesting food much faster than normal
options.B: Gastric acid is moving upward because the stomach valve is relaxed
options.C: The baby is kicking directly against her small intestine
options.D: Her liver is failing to produce enough bile for digestion

explanation: Hormones relax the valve at the top of the stomach, letting acid irritate the food pipe after eating. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T7#BMP212_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why does constipation occur frequently in pregnant women?

options.A: Women drink much less water during the second trimester
options.B: Slowed bowel transit allows more water to be absorbed from stool
options.C: The large intestine completely stops absorbing any liquid
options.D: Fetal waste mixes directly with maternal stool in the colon

explanation: Because food moves slowly through the colon, the body reabsorbs extra water, leaving the stool hard and difficult to pass. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T7#BMP212_U1_T7_h4)

question: What relationship exists between pregnancy constipation and hemorrhoids?

options.A: Hemorrhoids block the colon and cause food to back up into the stomach
options.B: Straining from hard stools and pelvic pressure worsens swollen rectal veins
options.C: Constipation cures hemorrhoids by reducing blood flow to the lower bowel
options.D: Hemorrhoids prevent progesterone from affecting the large intestine

explanation: Hard stools lead to straining, which, combined with growing pelvic pressure, causes veins around the rectum to swell. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T7#BMP212_U1_T7_h4)

question: Where does the growing uterus push the stomach during pregnancy?

options.A: Upward and slightly to the left

explanation: As the uterus grows, it physically displaces the stomach upward and to the left of its normal position. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T7#BMP212_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why is knowing about organ displacement important when assessing a pregnant woman with right-sided abdominal pain?

options.A: The stomach moves into the pelvis, causing lower abdominal cramps
options.B: The liver shrinks to make room for the displaced small intestines
options.C: The gallbladder stops producing bile because it is compressed
options.D: The appendix moves upward, changing where pain from appendicitis might be felt

explanation: Because organs shift upward, conditions like appendicitis may not present with standard lower right quadrant pain. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T7#BMP212_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which dietary advice is most helpful for reducing heartburn during pregnancy?

options.A: Eating only once a day to rest the stomach
options.B: Eating small, frequent meals throughout the day
options.C: Consuming large meals right before going to bed
options.D: Eliminating all liquids from the daily diet

explanation: Smaller meals prevent the stomach from becoming overly full, reducing the chance of acid flowing back into the esophagus. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T7#BMP212_U1_T7_h6)

question: A pregnant woman complains of severe constipation despite drinking water. What additional non-medical advice should the midwife give?

options.A: Stop eating all forms of carbohydrates completely
options.B: Take strong commercial laxatives every morning before breakfast
options.C: Increase intake of local fiber-rich foods like vegetables and fruits
options.D: Lie flat on the back for two hours after every meal

explanation: Adding dietary fiber adds bulk to stool and helps stimulate normal bowel movements alongside adequate fluid intake. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T7#BMP212_U1_T7_h6)
